claim: OpenAI Agents SDK's three core primitives are Agents (LLM + instructions + tools), Handoffs (task delegation between agents), and Guardrails (parallel input/output validation that can abort execution early).
stance_target: rigid evals and safety-net architecture for agent frameworks (Pillar 1)
quoted_support: Guardrails: Safety nets are used to validate inputs to agents... Provides input validation and safety checks that run parallel to your agents and can break execution early if checks fail.

claim: Among the four compared frameworks, LangGraph alone is rated as having first-class, sophisticated state persistence via graph structures with conditional-edge transitions and LangSmith-integrated debugging, at the cost of the steepest learning curve.
stance_target: framework selection for complex, stateful director/worker orchestration (Pillar 5)
quoted_support: LangGraph: Excels in managing state through graph structures. Transitions are sophisticated, leveraging conditional edges, and debugging is well-supported via LangSmith integration.

claim: OpenAI Agents SDK has 'limited built-in support' for parallel multi-agent execution compared to LangGraph (good via graph structure) and AutoGen (supported via agent networks).
stance_target: OpenAI Agents SDK as the default choice for highly parallel director/worker fleets (Pillar 5)
quoted_support: OpenAI Agents SDK: Strong in agent handoffs but lacks built-in parallel execution.

claim: AutoGen's human-in-the-loop support is comparatively limited to three modes only: never, always, or at-termination intervention, versus LangGraph's ability to intervene at any point in the workflow.
quoted_support: Human-in-the-Loop Support... LangGraph: Very flexible, intervention at any point... AutoGen: Limited (never, always, or at termination)
